The physician may be found liable if the neck was treated in simultaneous hyperrotation and extension. That combined end-range position stresses the vertebral arteries and can cause vertebrobasilar ischemia, which fits the confusion, nausea, and vertigo after treatment in an elderly patient. I'm taking this from the team note, which lists it as one of two candidate answers. I chose it over prior treatment for cervical osteoarthritis because that history alone wouldn't make the physician negligent.
